tour.overview:
In the 1840s Emperor Pedro II of Brazil founded a summer town in the cool mountains above Rio, where the imperial court escaped the heat and yellow fever of the capital. Petrópolis grew into a town of palaces, gardens and canals lined with hydrangeas. Its summer palace is now the Imperial Museum, which holds the crown of Pedro II, and the emperor and empress rest in its neo-Gothic cathedral.

This private day trip takes you there with a licensed guide and a car, about an hour and a half from Rio up the Serra da Estrela through the Atlantic rainforest. You see the museum, the cathedral, the Crystal Palace, the house of the aviation pioneer Alberto Santos Dumont and the vast Quitandinha.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Rio de Janeiro
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Imperial Museum.
• The cathedral of St Peter of Alcantara.
• The Crystal Palace.
• Santos Dumont’s house, the Encantada.
• The Quitandinha palace.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your car and guide link the scattered sights of Petrópolis and let you stop on the mountain road, and the town is a cool break from the heat of Rio.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, families and travellers who have seen the sights of Rio.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer the coast, choose our 2-day trip to Paraty.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Imperial Museum is closed on Mondays; the tour then visits the Rio Negro palace instead. Petrópolis is 10 degrees cooler than Rio: bring a layer.

days.name: The Imperial Museum, the cathedral, the Crystal Palace, Santos Dumont's house and the Quitandinha
days.description:
What to expect: Brazil's imperial past in the mountains above Rio, with a licensed guide, private car and tickets.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:30 and drive north out of Rio and up the Serra da Estrela, a winding road through the Atlantic rainforest with views back to Guanabara Bay. In Petrópolis you start at the Imperial Museum, the pink neoclassical summer palace of Pedro II. In rooms of imperial furniture, portraits and the emperor's telescope, you see the imperial crown of Pedro II, made in 1841 for his coronation at the age of 15, with 639 diamonds and 77 pearls. Visitors slide over the precious wooden floors in felt slippers.

You then visit the cathedral of St Peter of Alcantara, a neo-Gothic church whose imperial chapel holds the tombs of Pedro II and Empress Teresa Cristina, brought back from exile in 1921. After lunch (not included), you see the Crystal Palace, an iron and glass pavilion made in France in 1884 and given by Princess Isabel's husband; it was here that Isabel celebrated the freeing of slaves in the town before the abolition of slavery in 1888.

You continue to the Encantada, the small house built by Alberto Santos Dumont, the Brazilian aviation pioneer, with its steep stairs designed so you start each step on the right foot and the alcohol-heated shower he invented. Before driving back to Rio you stop at the Quitandinha palace, a Norman-style hotel-casino of 1944 that closed when gambling was banned in 1946, with its vast halls and a dome over a lake-shaped lounge.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up in Rio.
10:00 – Imperial Museum.
11:45 – Cathedral of St Peter of Alcantara.
12:30 – Lunch break.
14:00 – Crystal Palace.
14:30 – Santos Dumont’s house.
15:15 – Quitandinha palace.
16:00 – Drive back to Rio.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A craft beer tasting at a local brewery can be added; Petrópolis is known for its beer.
• Lunch in a former imperial residence or a mountain restaurant can be arranged.
• The museum is closed on Mondays.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: About 1 hour 30 minutes each way, depending on traffic.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Imperial Museum, the cathedral and Santos Dumont’s house.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No. Your guide suggests a restaurant in the historic centre.

faq.question: Can photos be taken in the Imperial Museum?
faq.answer: Photography inside is restricted; the gardens and exteriors can be photographed freely.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the slippers in the museum and Santos Dumont’s inventions. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The museum is on one main floor; Santos Dumont’s house has very steep stairs.

faq.question: Can we add a brewery visit?
faq.answer: Yes. Petrópolis has several craft breweries, including a historic one in the town.

faq.question: Can we combine Petrópolis with hiking?
faq.answer: Yes. The Serra dos Órgãos national park nearby has trails with views of the Dedo de Deus peak.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and a warm layer for the mountains.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. April to September is dry and cool; the hydrangeas bloom from November to January.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Brazil but never required. If you were happy with your guide and driver, a small tip at the end of the day is a kind gesture.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
